idiom_name: MutableMap.getOrPut on the JVM; android.util.LruCache on Android; Caffeine for production
implementation_notes: Kotlin inherits the Java cache ecosystem, so the pattern arrives as a library: Caffeine or Guava on the JVM, platform classes on Android, with Kotlin adding ergonomics rather than machinery. A MutableMap with getOrPut expresses cache-aside in one expression, and a delegated property (val x by lazy { ... }) covers the single-value case where the whole cache is one lazily populated field. On Android, android.util.LruCache is the platform cache with sizeOf()/entryRemoved() hooks and trimMemory cooperation. The classic structure - hand-written hash table plus recency list - is written only in library-free, allocation-sensitive code.
pitfalls: getOrPut on a plain MutableMap is not atomic: two threads can both run the loader, and concurrent put() calls corrupt a LinkedHashMap-backed map - use ConcurrentHashMap.computeIfAbsent for shared caches.
Mutable keys break lookups: keys must be immutable data classes with a stable hashCode, or entries become unreachable.
Android LruCache sizes entries in the units sizeOf() reports; forgetting to override sizeOf makes it count entries while maxSize is budgeted in bytes.
by lazy defaults to synchronized for thread safety, which serializes initialisation; LazyThreadSafetyMode.NONE is an explicit choice, not a default.
